title: The 8 Best Plunge Router Bits 2026
metaDescription: Our 8 picks for plunge router bits 2026, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at plunge router bits 2026 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Freud 75-100 Up Spiral Bit, 1/8-Inch
products.blurb: Key specs: Spiral up-cut geometry, Center-cutting end, TiCo carbide.
strengths: Center-cutting end allows plunging directly into the surface without a pilot hole
Spiral up-cut geometry produces a shearing action that dramatically reduces tearout
TiCo carbide stays sharp longer than standard carbide in repeated plunge cuts
The most commonly recommended plunge bit for stopped grooves and mortises
limitations: Up-cut spiral pulls chips upward -- some chip ejection onto the workpiece surface
Higher price than standard straight plunge bits
products.bestFor: buyers who want the best overall package

products.name: Freud 76-102 Down Spiral Bit, 1/4-Inch
products.blurb: Key specs: Down-cut spiral, Pushes chips into the cut, TiCo Hi-Density carbide.
strengths: Down-cut spiral pushes chips downward into the kerf -- keeps the workpiece surface clean
The correct choice for plunge cuts in veneered plywood and laminate where the top surface is visible
TiCo carbide construction for strong edge retention
Clean, crisp entry on the top face that an up-cut bit cannot match
limitations: Down-cut geometry is less efficient at chip removal -- more heat in the cut
Higher price than a comparable up-cut bit
Not ideal for deep cuts due to chip packing

products.name: Freud 75-103 Up Spiral Bit, 1/4-Inch
products.blurb: Key specs: 1/4-inch diameter, Center-cutting, TiCo Hi-Density carbide.
strengths: A common everyday diameter for stopped grooves and shallow mortises
TiCo carbide for strong edge retention in repeated plunge cuts
Sized for handheld routing where a compact bit is easier to control
A practical companion size alongside the 1/8-inch bit for a range of groove widths
limitations: Single fixed diameter -- doesn't cover wider mortises

products.name: YONICO 14320 CNC End Mill Solid Carbide Up Cut Set, 3 Bit
products.blurb: Key specs: Multiple sizes in set, Up-cut spiral, Center-cutting.
strengths: Set provides multiple plunge bit sizes in one purchase for the price of a single premium bit
Good starting set for new woodworkers learning mortising and stopped-groove routing
Yonico carbide is adequate for softwood and plywood
Center-cutting geometry on all bits in the set
limitations: Yonico carbide dulls faster than Freud or Amana in hardwood
Cut quality is lower than premium bits -- more tearout in hardwood

products.name: CMT 653.158.11 Insert Carbide Straight Router Bit, 5/8-Inch
products.blurb: Key specs: Center-cutting straight bit, Two-flute design, Micro-grain carbide.
strengths: Straight flutes are the correct choice for plunge cuts in inlay recesses where parallel walls matter
Anti-kickback body reduces the risk of catches when starting a plunge cut
CMT micro-grain carbide provides better edge retention than standard carbide
Flat bottom makes it correct for hinge mortises and shallow recesses
limitations: Straight flutes produce more tearout than spiral geometry in many hardwoods

products.name: Amana Tool 49310 Special Rabbet Plunge Bit
products.blurb: Key specs: Center-cutting, Carbide-tipped, Flat bottom.
strengths: Amana carbide is harder than standard carbide and holds an edge through repeated plunge cuts
Center-cutting capability for direct plunge without pilot hole
Flat bottom for accurate recess depth
A distinct special-rabbet profile useful for stepped hardware mortises
limitations: Straight geometry -- more tearout than spiral in difficult grain

products.name: Freud 16-520 Mortising Bit, 3/4-Inch
products.blurb: Key specs: 3/4-inch mortising bit, Perma-SHIELD coating, TiCo carbide.
strengths: Purpose-built for mortise routing -- the most common plunge routing application
3/4-inch width matches common tenon thicknesses in furniture-scale joinery
TiCo carbide produces clean mortise walls without tearout in most hardwoods
Perma-SHIELD coating reduces friction and pitch buildup during repeated plunge cuts
limitations: Single fixed width -- buy additional bits for other tenon thicknesses
Mortise-specific -- less versatile than a general spiral plunge bit

products.name: Freud 77-208 Double Compression Bit, 1/2-Inch
products.blurb: Key specs: Compression spiral geometry, Up-cut at bottom, down-cut at top, TiCo Hi-Density carbide.
strengths: Compression spiral is both up-cut at the bottom (clean floor) and down-cut at the top (clean surface) simultaneously
Produces clean cuts on both faces of a panel -- correct for veneered plywood routed on a CNC or with a plunge router
TiCo Hi-Density carbide with Black I.C.E. coating for extended tool life
Eliminates the need to choose between up-cut and down-cut when both faces are critical
limitations: Higher price than a single-direction spiral bit
Primarily a CNC-oriented bit -- requires consistent feed rate for best performance
Less common in hand-held plunge routing
features: Up-cut at bottom, down-cut at top

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
